title: fix: improve Kontext failure attribution
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
## Summary

- Preserve true Azure HTTP status, response headers, and request IDs for Kontext failures.
- Map explicit no-image content filters and moderation-worded Azure HTTP errors to `422 content_policy_violation`, while retaining the real upstream status.
- Return `502` for other HTTP-200/no-image responses and record a structural response summary that excludes prompt, image URL, and base64 fields.
- Require official-model failures across multiple keys/users, or a matching-surface synthetic probe, before declaring `DEGRADED`.

## Why

The Kontext alert reported 17 “Azure 500s,” but all 17 came from one user/key using the same reference image. That key also had 15 successes, other callers were healthy, and a direct edit probe against the production Azure route returned a valid image.

The adapter was turning an Azure HTTP 200 response without `data[0].b64_json` into a generic local 500 and discarding the response shape. The monitor then treated the concentrated caller-specific cluster as an official outage. This fixes both sources of misattribution without changing the route, credentials, pricing, or success response.

## Verification

- `npx vitest run test/image/azureFluxKontextModel.test.ts` — 6 passed
- `npm run typecheck` — passed
- Biome and `git diff --check` — passed

gist.headline: The hive reads the receipt
gist.blurb: Kontext failures now keep their upstream paperwork instead of arriving dressed as generic 500s. The monitor also learned that one troublesome flowerpot is not necessarily a garden-wide drought.
gist.summary: The Azure Flux Kontext adapter now preserves upstream HTTP status, headers, and request IDs; maps explicit no-image content-filter responses to 422 content_policy_violation; returns 502 with a scrubbed structural response summary for other HTTP-200/no-image results; and requires failures across users or a matching probe before marking the official model DEGRADED.
gist.impact: Users get more accurate Kontext error handling and content-policy signals, while operators can distinguish isolated caller-specific failures from a real Azure route outage without exposing prompts, image URLs, or base64 data.
gist.visual_concept: Depict Kontext response diagnosis as a cozy garden clinic: Polli compares several neatly labeled request receipts from different garden paths while a healthy code-plant blooms beside one wilted pot, showing that a single bad response is not a platform-wide outage. Include a retro CRT monitor robot displaying a simple pixel response shape and a friendly 422 content-policy sign, with no real prompt or image data shown.
